## ✨ Highlights

The first steps of the beta: what it covers, the pace releases keep and the support they get - and a security update of the Controller's updater.

- 🔒 **The Controller's updater: Docker Compose v5.7.0** ([#509](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/509)) - its Go runtime had a critical and four high HTTP/2 vulnerabilities.
- 🧭 **What Janus supports, said everywhere** ([#528](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/528)): amd64 virtual machines on KVM/libvirt and Proxmox VE, with or without the Controller - the rest is experimental.
- 🩹 **Maintenance releases** ([#529](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/529), [#533](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/533)): the previous release keeps getting security fixes for 14 days after the next one ships, and the Controller offers them to its nodes.
- 🛡️ **The Controller's Content Security Policy is enforced** ([#531](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/531)).

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Update your Controllers to this release.** Until now a Controller took GitHub's first release for the newest. A maintenance release - none exists yet - is tagged after the newest release and comes first in GitHub's list, and a Controller before this release would take it for the latest. Then `docker compose up -d` once, for the updater's security fix (🔒 below): an update doesn't replace the updater's own image.
- **The Content Security Policy now blocks**: a page loading anything from another origin, or running an inline script, is refused by the browser. The Controller's pages load nothing of the kind; a browser extension that injects scripts into them may stop working there. The Controller logs what browsers report blocked: `csp: "<page>" blocked "<directive>": "<what>"`.

## 🔒 Security

- **Docker Compose v5.6.1 → v5.7.0** (the Controller's updater, `janus-controller-updater`) - fixes of the Go standard library it was built with, in `net/http`'s HTTP/2:
  - 🔴 critical [CVE-2026-78663](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6612) - double flow control refund on HTTP/2 server streams
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-78659](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6603) - HTTP/2 server memory exhaustion due to Trailer headers
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-78660](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6610) - HTTP/2 transport accepts malformed framing-related headers
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-78669](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6611) - excessive CPU consumption from repeated initial window changes
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-97032](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6617) - HTTP/2 server crash due to an HPACK encoder race

  The updater has no network of its own (`network_mode: none`) and speaks only to Docker's socket: these can't be reached from outside. **Updating the Controller doesn't update its updater**: the updater keeps the image it started with. Update the Controller, then run `docker compose up -d` in its Compose directory - the updater restarts on the new image, which is harmless at any time ([updating the Controller](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/dashboard/README.md)). `docker exec janus-controller-updater /usr/local/bin/docker-compose version` says v5.7.0 once it's done.
- **golang.org/x/net v0.61.0 → v0.62.0** - [CVE-2026-78661](https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GO-2026-6860) and [CVE-2026-97045](https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GO-2026-6866), unrated, in its `html` package: only the image factory's website uses it, never a node, janusctl or the Controller. Nothing to do.

## 🖥️ Controller

- **Maintenance releases offered to the nodes on the release they fix** ([#533](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/533)): on a node's **System › Update** page, under the update, **Maintenance release vX of vY** - its security fixes without the newer release's changes. **Use this maintenance release** fills the usual A/B installation in; for a node with extensions the image factory builds it first. The update offered stays the newest release.
- **Releases ordered by version** ([#529](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/529)): GitHub lists them by the date of each tag's commit. The Controller and the image factory now sort them by version, and the 🔒 badge leaves out the fixes a node's own release already carries.
- **Content Security Policy enforced** ([#531](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/531)) on the page, the API and every node's page - it was report-only since the 2026-10-07 security review. What it allows is in [the Controller's UI design](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/controller-ui.md#content-security-policy).
- **A node joining the fleet shows as joining** ([#523](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/523)), not as trusted with an error, for the moments it takes the fleet's trust after its admission.
- **A refusal after a connection cut short is reported at once** ([#524](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/524)): the Controller retried a node that had refused its certificate until a 30 s deadline - the cause of `TestRenewTheFleet`'s CI failures.
- **Links in a notice readable in every palette** ([#532](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/532)): eleven palettes' accent was a hair under AA contrast on a notice's tint - the cluster lock's link on a node page, for one.

## 🩹 Releases and support

- **The previous release is supported for 14 days** after the next one ships ([security policy](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions)): a vulnerability fixed then gets a maintenance release of it - that release with the fix, nothing else. Its version is one of that release's day, after it (`v2026.11.10-2` for a `v2026.11.10`), it is named "maintenance of" it and never marked the latest ([maintenance releases](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/updates.md#maintenance-releases)). A release followed the same day by the next has no such version left - this one's own predecessor, v2026.11.04, for one.
- **A release pace beta testers can follow**: releases are pre-released and tested on the lab first, then promoted at most once a week - a security fix doesn't wait.

## 🧭 Docs and site

- **What Janus supports** ([#528](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/528)): [a page](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/private-cloud/README.md#what-janus-supports) the README, the provisioning guide and the platform pages point to - amd64 VMs on KVM/libvirt and Proxmox VE are supported, bare metal, VMware ESXi, the Raspberry Pi, arm64 nodes and other hypervisors experimental. The image builder marks each platform **supported** or **experimental**.
